importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types — a bamboo eco-resort hut, a GI sheet security cabin, and a PUF panel labour accommodation are visually unrecognisable as the same product category. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Material/panel type, use application, and size are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria — a PUF-insulated site office and a GI sheet security cabin cannot substitute for each other. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by procurement buyers.

Indian construction contractors compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively across sellers once material and use type are confirmed. Price delta between PUF panel and GI sheet huts is substantial — spec tier drives price, making this a spec-driven comparison signal.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard fixed-size security cabins and guard huts are also quoted per piece; both units are active in this MCAT. Per sq ft is dominant for custom labour camps and site offices. Unit must always be shown alongside price to prevent misreading.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece ambiguity is documented and real — a 10x20 ft hut quoted per piece vs per sq ft creates a price comparison error of 200x. Price cannot be interpreted without unit clarity.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — Tata Steel's Nest-In/MobiNest is a notable entrant but buyers do not search by brand name; market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by spec and price.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer status, installation capability, and IS compliance track record matter for large institutional orders but are evaluated after spec and price shortlisting, not before.

top_configurator_specs.reason: PUF panel vs EPS panel vs sheet cladding defines the thermal performance tier and drives the largest price delta in this category — non-interchangeable across insulation requirements.
Each use type (security cabin, labour hut, site office, toilet block) requires a different structural configuration and fitting set — non-interchangeable and the primary product variant selector.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers specify PUF panel thickness (40mm / 50mm / 60mm / 75mm) as a direct thermal performance and cost driver — the existing Insulation spec captures layer count only, not the thickness dimension that determines price.

Site office and labour hut buyers specify whether basic wiring, full electrical fittings, or no electrical is included — this materially affects price and determines whether the seller can supply a turnkey unit.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Material defines the construction system and price tier — sellers need this to confirm they manufacture in the requested material and to provide an accurate per-sq-ft rate.
Floor area is the primary cost driver for custom-built huts — sellers need this to calculate material quantity and provide a meaningful price.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need the intended application (security cabin, labour hut, site office, toilet block) to confirm they supply the right structural configuration and fittings, and to price the unit accurately.
